card.name: "When" before co-administered drug
card.fires_on: The word "when" in drug interaction text, right before a named drug is given, mixed, started or stopped together with another drug. It also fires on a few similar linking words such as "are" before "mixed", or "if" clauses.

modes.label: When before co-use
modes.description: "when" follows a statement about effect or dose change and introduces co-administration with a named drug.
modes.example: drugs that are metabolized by these enzyme systems may have lower than expected plasma levels<< when>> co-administered with nevirap

modes.label: Other linking words
modes.description: Other linking words in interaction text, such as "are" before "mixed" or "symptoms" before "if misused".
modes.example: precipitation can occur when eye drops containing thimerosal<< are>> mixed with ROCKLATAN.

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about placing or combining one thing with another, but the output effect is weak.
card.plain: It marks the point in an interaction warning where the text says what happens when two drugs are used together.
